title: Urinary System
shortDescription: The kidneys' internal structure, the nephron's role, and the full path from blood filtration to urine excretion.
genZNote: Filter today for a healthier tomorrow — the kidneys are the body's water and waste managers.

structures.name: Kidney
structures.description: Paired, bean-shaped organs behind the abdominal cavity.

structures.name: Renal cortex
structures.function: Contains most of the nephrons' filtering structures.

structures.name: Renal pelvis
structures.function: Collects urine before it drains into the ureter.

structures.name: Renal artery
structures.description: Vessel bringing blood into the kidney.

structures.name: Renal vein
structures.description: Vessel carrying filtered blood away from the kidney.

structures.name: Ureter
structures.description: Tube running from each kidney to the bladder.
structures.function: Carries urine from the kidney to the bladder.
structures.highYield: Kidney → bladder — there are two of these, one per kidney.

structures.name: Urethra
structures.description: Single tube from the bladder to outside the body.
structures.function: Carries urine out of the body.
structures.highYield: Bladder → outside the body — only one, unlike the paired ureters.

pathways.title: Urine Formation and Excretion
steps: Urine → ureter → bladder → urethra → out of the body

comparisons.distinction: Ureters (x2) carry urine from each kidney to the bladder; the urethra (x1) carries urine from the bladder out of the body.
Filtration moves substances from blood into the nephron; reabsorption moves useful substances back from the nephron into the blood — opposite directions.

questions.prompt: Which structure carries urine OUT of the body?
questions.explanation: The urethra carries urine from the bladder out of the body. Ureters carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
optionNotes: Carries urine from kidney to bladder, not out of the body.
Collects urine inside the kidney before the ureter.

questions.prompt: In the labelled kidney illustration, which region is the outer layer that contains most of the filtering structures?
questions.explanation: The renal cortex is the kidney's outer region and contains most of the nephrons' filtering structures.
optionNotes: The inner region, involved in concentrating urine.
Carries urine away from the kidney, doesn't filter.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of urine formation?
questions.explanation: Urine formation proceeds filtration → reabsorption → secretion, fine-tuning the final composition of urine at each step.
optionNotes: Reabsorption cannot happen before filtration has occurred.
Reabsorption comes before secretion in the correct sequence.

sections.heading: Structures of the Urinary System
bullets: Kidneys — a pair of bean-shaped organs that filter blood and form urine.
Renal cortex — the kidney's outer region.
Renal medulla — the kidney's inner region.
Renal pelvis — the funnel-shaped area that collects urine before it leaves the kidney.
Nephron — the kidney's microscopic functional unit, where filtration actually happens.
Renal artery and renal vein — bring blood to and from each kidney.
Ureters — tubes carrying urine from each kidney to the bladder.
Urinary bladder — stores urine until elimination.
Urethra — the tube through which urine leaves the body.

steps.name: Filtration
steps.explanation: Blood pressure forces water, salts, glucose, and waste out of the blood and into the nephron.
steps.purpose: Separates small dissolved substances from blood cells and large proteins, which stay in the blood.

steps.name: Reabsorption
steps.explanation: Useful substances (glucose, most water, needed ions) are reabsorbed back into the blood from the nephron.
steps.purpose: Prevents the body from losing nutrients it still needs.

steps.name: Secretion
steps.explanation: Additional waste products and excess ions are actively added into the forming urine from the blood.
steps.purpose: Fine-tunes the final composition of urine, including pH balance.

sections.heading: Pathway and Roles
sections.body:
Blood → kidney → urine, i.e. blood enters the kidney, is filtered by nephrons, and the waste-containing fluid becomes urine, which travels kidney → ureter → bladder → urethra → out of the body.

Beyond waste removal, the kidneys regulate fluid balance (how much water the body retains) and electrolyte balance (sodium, potassium, and other ion levels).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The urinary system filters blood through the kidneys' nephrons to remove waste and excess fluid as urine, which passes through the ureters, bladder, and urethra.
keyFacts: The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney, where filtration, reabsorption, and secretion occur.
Urine pathway: kidney → ureter → bladder → urethra.
Each kidney has an outer renal cortex and inner renal medulla, draining into the renal pelvis.
The kidneys regulate both waste removal and fluid/electrolyte balance.
commonConfusion: Ureter (kidney → bladder) is easily confused with urethra (bladder → outside the body) due to their similar names.
Filtration (removing substances from blood into the nephron) is often confused with reabsorption (returning useful substances back to blood) — they move in opposite directions.

highYieldFacts: Ureters carry urine FROM the kidneys TO the bladder; the urethra carries urine OUT of the bladder.
Glucose is normally fully reabsorbed and should not appear in healthy urine.
commonTraps: Don't mix up "ureter" and "urethra" — spelling and function are both commonly tested together.
Filtration happens in the nephron's glomerulus, not directly in the renal pelvis.
mustRemember: Urine formation order: filtration → reabsorption → secretion.
Full pathway: blood → nephron (kidney) → ureter → bladder → urethra → out.

confusedTerms.distinction: Ureters connect each kidney to the bladder; the urethra is the single tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body.
